definition: Scant means barely sufficient — so little that it falls short of what is needed.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word scant. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know scant should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The detective had only scant evidence: a single blurry footprint by the gate.
A slim supply is small but might still stretch far enough; a scant supply falls short of what's actually needed.
Scant evidence is at least some evidence; nonexistent evidence is none at all.

Minimal means the least possible amount, often pared down on purpose — minimal packaging, minimal fuss. It suggests a floor deliberately reached. Scant is about accident and shortfall: less than the situation needs, with nobody choosing it. A minimal design succeeds by using little; scant evidence fails by having little.

Negligible means so small it hardly counts and can safely be ignored — a negligible fee, a negligible risk. Scant amounts still count; they are just not enough. Scant attention is real attention that falls short of what is needed; negligible attention might as well be none.

Slight means small in degree — a slight delay, a slight accent, a slight improvement — measuring how far something departs from zero or from normal. Scant measures against need: scant evidence, scant hope, scant regard are amounts that fall short of what the moment requires.

Scant means barely sufficient — so little that it falls short of what is needed.
The teacher's proposal received scant attention at the crowded staff meeting; only two colleagues even looked up.
Scant fits because the amount of attention was far less than the proposal needed — barely any at all.
Scant most often sits right before an abstract noun: scant attention, scant evidence, scant regard, scant hope.

It's a close cousin of meager, another word in this unit — both mean 'barely enough,' but scant stresses falling just short of a needed amount, while meager stresses thin, inadequate quality (a meager meal).
Scant can even mean 'just barely' with measurements: 'a scant teaspoon of salt.'

The community theater won the rights to the musical in March — on the condition that it open by the first Friday of May.
That left scant rehearsal time: five weekends to stage a show that professional companies polish for months.
The director cut nothing and rushed nothing; instead she listed what the show truly needed and gave every hour to that list.
Ensemble numbers got whole Saturdays.
A minor scene change the audience would never study got twenty minutes and a prayer.
On opening night the harmonies held.
What they'd had was never enough time — but it had gone exactly where the need was.
